components.css: .ds-lane { color: var(--foreground); padding: 14px 8px; width: 360px; } .ds-lane-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; } .ds-lane-no { width: 24px; height: 24px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 4px; background: var(--foreground); color: var(--background); font-weight: 900; font-size: 13px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-lane-name { flex: 1; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-lane-pct { font-size: 17px; font-weight: 800; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-lane-track { position: relative; height: 28px; margin-top: 10px; background: var(--surface); border-top: 2px solid var(--lane); border-bottom: 2px solid var(--lane); } .ds-lane-fill { height: 100%; width: 82%; background: var(--warning); } .ds-lane-curb { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; left: 75%; border-left: 2px dashed var(--lane); } .ds-lane-finish { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; left: calc(100% - 8px); width: 8px; background: repeating-conic-gradient(var(--foreground) 0 25%, var(--background) 0 50%) 0 0 / 8px 8px; } .ds-lane-meta { margin-top: 8px; font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted-foreground); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

narrative.overview:
Anton is set like the printed lane sheet of a 1976 Montréal track meet: a deep ultramarine ink ground, a saturated royal-blue rail down the left, warm-white type, and bold grotesque numerals that read at a glance. The identity lends type, palette, density and exactly one move; the product stays a plain working dashboard. There is one fixed dark theme and no light mode.

Density is moderate. Structure comes from hairline rules and row dividers rather than nested cards: a page is a few bordered modules whose rows are separated by lines. Numbers are the loudest thing on the screen (a 64px weekly distance, a 17px percent on every lane), and the interface around them is quiet. Azure is the single chromatic signal at rest; green, amber and red appear only as wear state, and orange only as Strava provenance.

The signature is the numbered track lane: each pair near its limit is drawn as a lane with white lane lines top and bottom, a dashed curb at 75% of the limit, and a chequered finish line at the limit.
keyCharacteristics: One fixed dark ultramarine theme; depth by tonal step and hairline, not shadow.
One typeface family for display and UI (Schibsted Grotesk, weights 700-900 for emphasis), one mono for raw data.
Tabular numerals wherever numbers are compared.
Royal-blue rail and mobile top bar frame content; the active nav item is a solid warm-white tab.
Same components from 380 px phone to wide desktop; PWA safe-area insets honored.

rules.name: The Traffic-Light Rule
rules.body: Wear is green under 75% of a shoe's limit, amber from 75% to 100%, red beyond. The thresholds are product rules, not styling. The lane curb sits at 75% of the limit and the finish at 100%.

rules.name: The Strava Rule
rules.body: Strava Orange marks Strava-sourced runs and nothing else.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Azure is the only chromatic voice at rest. Green, amber and red appear only when a wear state earns them.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that may be compared across rows or over time uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Flat-Tonal Rule
rules.body: To lift an element, step it up one surface tone or add a hairline; do not add shadow or glow.

dos: Do use only the CSS variables through Tailwind tokens; add a token before adding a color.
Do keep wear state on the Traffic-Light Rule: green under 75%, amber 75-100%, red beyond.
Do let Strava Orange mark Strava-sourced runs only.
Do separate rows with Divider lines and hairlines instead of nesting cards.
Do use tabular numerals for mileage, pace, price and dates.
Do keep the 2px azure focus ring on every interactive element.
Do check every screen at desktop and about 380 px, with safe-area insets in the installed PWA.
donts: Don't add a light theme or a `.dark` toggle; the system is one fixed dark theme.
Don't use shadows, glows or gradients to create hierarchy; step the surface tone.
Don't hard-code colors in components; the chequered finish strip and image placeholder stripes read from variables or the shared utility.
Don't add a second display typeface; weight and size carry hierarchy.
Don't introduce another chart library or heavy UI dependency; charts stay on recharts.
